newsitem.title: GERMANY: German barge traffic flows only slightly reduced.
newsitem.headline: German barge traffic flows only slightly reduced.

text.p: Most of Germany's barge trade is intact despite the closure of the Elbe and Oder rivers and estuaries due to high water levels, the shippers organisation BDB (Bundesverband der Deutschen Binnenschiffahrt) said.
"Current waterway closures take out only a few percent of total traffic volumes," managing director Gerhard von Haus said in response to an enquiry.
Shipping has been suspended on the two rivers connecting Germany with Poland and the Czech Republic following heavy rains.
Von Haus said the closures did not extend to key mineral oil routes while incoming supplies from Poland were mostly construction materials.
The amount of grain, feeds, ores or metals in the blocked traffic was also small.
BDB represents some 3,000 vessels in the 500-3,000 tonne category, the bulk of the German-owned inland barge fleet.

Officials at the German compound feed industry association (FFMI) said some southern European shipments of feed grain and other raw materials to the west may have been disrupted when Danube shipping was suspended in Austria on Sunday.
On Monday, the Passau-Linz route was re-opened but an eastern stretch running to the Slovak border remained closed.
